about: Parasitics of passive parts in a signal channel (series resistors, AC-coupling capacitors, terminations), per package. The package comes from the footprint name (KiCad library names such as C_0805_2012Metric, IPC-7351 names, plain imperial codes) or else from the pad geometry (nearest standard land pattern by pad pitch and pad width, kisi_board::package). All values are typical estimates for chip parts on a PCB, not from a specific datasheet; replace them with Touchstone data of the actual part when it matters.

sources.text: Typical body ESL and pad capacitance of chip resistors and MLCCs by case size, consistent with vendor application notes (Murata, KEMET, Vishay) for 0201–1210; estimated. 1210: body ESL as in decoupling.esl_nh, pad capacitance as for larger parts.

decoupling.about: Decoupling capacitors in the PDN model: body ESL and ESR per package, DC-bias derating of class II MLCCs, assumed rated voltage when the value text has none, and the parts the recommendations choose from. Typical values; a PI_CAP field in <board>.kisi.json (ESR, ESL, rated voltage, dielectric, capacitance at bias from the datasheet) replaces them per part.

sources.text: I. Novak et al., DesignCon East 2011, as quoted by EPCI (passive-components.eu, 'High CV MLCC DC Bias and Ageing Capacitance Loss Explained'): 10 µF 0805 6.3 V MLCCs of three vendors lose 12–32 % at 3.3 V and 35–65 % at rated voltage; X5R at 5 V about −60 %.
F. Janssen, Maxim Integrated application note 6014 'How to Measure Capacity Versus Bias Voltage on MLCCs' (2014): a 10 µF MLCC keeps 66–67 % at 5 V.

Body ESL by case size and ESR(C) trend: typical MLCC values consistent with vendor application notes (Murata, KEMET, TDK); the 'standard' derating curve (low capacitance for the case size) is a kisi estimate between class I (no loss) and the high-CV data above.

mount_nh.note: mounting inductance assumed for recommended parts: vias at the pads to the planes

dc_bias.note: capacitance retention C(V)/C(0) over V / rated voltage for class II dielectrics (X5R, X7R, X6S, X7S, Y5V); class I (C0G/NP0), polymer, tantalum and electrolytic keep their value

rated_v.note: rated voltage assumed when neither the value text nor PI_CAP gives one: the smallest standard rating ≥ margin × rail voltage

series.about: Series parts in a supply path (resistors up to r_max_ohm, inductors, ferrite beads) in the PDN model: the rail domain runs through them up to the regulators. Typical values; a PI_SERIES field (r, dcr, l, z100, rp, lp, cp) or the r of a PI_REG pass stage replaces them per part.

sources.text: Ferrite bead as Rdc + (Lp ∥ Rp ∥ Cp), fitted to the impedance at 100 MHz given in the value ("600R@100MHz", Murata BLM part numbers) or z100_ohm: Lp so that ωLp = Z100 at 100 MHz, Rp = rp_factor·Z100, Cp from cp_pf; shape consistent with the impedance curves in vendor data (Murata BLM18 series, Würth WE-CBF). Without a rating, z100_ohm and rdc_ohm are estimates for a typical 0603 supply bead.

Chip inductor DC resistance by case size: typical for about 1–4.7 µH power inductors in vendor tables (Murata LQM, TDK MLP), estimate; parasitic capacitance not modelled. Resistor and jumper inductance: the capacitor ESL by case size.

thermal.about: Package thermal resistances for the temperature estimate (kisi_pi::thermal, two-resistor model JESD15-3: junction to board θJB, junction to case top θJC) when a part has no PI_THERMAL field. The family comes from the footprint name (first family whose pattern the name contains, case-insensitive), else from the pad geometry (an exposed centre pad: qfn; a grid of round pads: bga; two pads: chip), else generic. θ = θ_ref·(A_ref/A)^exp with A the area of the pads' bounding box in mm² (a stand-in for the package body). Values from one or two datasheets per family; every default is an estimate – the part's own datasheet (Thermal Information table) belongs in PI_THERMAL.
thermal.tj_max_note: assumed when PI_THERMAL gives no tj_max: a common limit of commercial ICs (commercial FPGAs are often 85 °C, power ICs 150 °C)

kisi estimate for two-pad chip parts (resistors, ferrites, …): a film at 155 °C at rated power and 70 °C (IEC 60115-1 rating convention) spends about half of that rise inside the part; 0603 (pad box ≈ 2.2 mm²) ≈ 150 K/W, scaled with the area; no top path
kisi estimate for parts of no known family (between the QFP/SO values for leaded and the QFN values for exposed-pad packages of a similar size)
